mainTopic: Seasonal land prices, how 'מיטב' and 'ישיב' fit together in paying damages, and how 'best' land is measured
overview: The amud opens inside an older discussion that אביי quotes. A landowner with no cash may take מעשר עני only up to half his land's value. רבה explains why: land is cheap in תשרי and expensive in ניסן, and it never drops more than half. אביי uses this seasonal idea to settle a contradiction in the פסוק between 'מיטב' (pay from the best land) and 'ישיב' (pay with anything). רב אחא בר יעקב rejects applying it to damages and moves it to a lender. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא rejects that too and moves it to a כתובה, so the original contradiction returns. רבא suggests that every payment must be the best of its kind. Because the פסוק says 'of his field,' the גמרא replaces his reading with another one: movables always count as 'best,' and only land must be top quality. Finally, רבי אבא rules that 'best' land is measured against the injurer's own fields, and רב שמואל בר אבא begins a challenge from a ברייתא about the three grades of land. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He should not get even a little
steps.stepSummary: The quoted discussion challenges the ruling that a landowner may take מעשר עני up to half his land's value. If he owns valuable land, why give him anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then we should not give him even a small amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא, in a discussion that אביי is quoting, attacks the rule that this landowner may take מעשר עני up to half the value of his land. If he owns land, he is not really poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule assumed this man counts as poor enough to take some מעשר עני, but only a limited amount. The challenge says that is inconsistent. If his land is worth a lot, he is not poor at all, and he should get nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: let them give him, provide him with
the tithe given to the poor

steps.confusionAlert: This is not אביי's own question about damages. It is part of an older discussion about מעשר עני that אביי is quoting so he can borrow its answer for נזקין.

phrases.english: Even a little, also
phrases.notes: "Him" is the poor man who owns a field and house. The "little" is a portion of מעשר עני.

phrases.english: they should not give him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ פּוּרְתָּא נָמֵי לָא לִיסְפּוֹ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted just before this section, which limits a landowner's מעשר עני to half his land's value.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a landowner may take מעשר עני up to half the value of his land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his land has real value, he is not poor and should not take any מעשר עני at all. A partial amount makes no sense.

steps.title: Land is expensive in ניסן and cheap in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the rule is needed for a case of seasonal prices: land is worth more in ניסן and less in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master (רבה) said about this: The rule is needed for this case. In the days of ניסן land is expensive, and in the days of תשרי land is cheap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins his answer. He says the ruling is about a special situation where land prices change with the seasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא צריכא means "the rule is needed for this specific case." רבה is changing how we picture the case. The man's land is not simply valuable or simply worthless. Its value depends on the season.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for this case; the rule is needed for a specific situation
the spring month / the autumn month

phrases.english: And the Master said about it:
It is needed only for this case:
that in the days of Nisan land is expensive,
and in the days of Tishrei land is cheap;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר עֲלַהּ: לָא צְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling applies where land prices change with the seasons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man's land has one fixed value, so he is either poor or not poor.
steps.terutzMaskana: His land's value changes by season, which allows a middle ruling.

steps.title: Why he may take up to half
steps.stepSummary: Most people wait until ניסן to sell. This man needs cash now, so he sells at the low תשרי price. Land drops by up to half and no more, so he may take מעשר עני up to half its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone waits until ניסן and then sells. But this man needs money, so he sells at today's price. Land normally drops by up to half its value, but not more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his answer and explains exactly where the "half" comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ניסן this man would not be poor, so he cannot take unlimited מעשר עני. But he is forced to sell in תשרי, and that loss is real. Since land never drops more than half, his loss is at most half, so he may take מעשר עני up to that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: at the current price, like now

steps.whatToRemember: Land is worth more in ניסן and less in תשרי, and it drops by up to half but no more. A forced seller in תשרי may take מעשר עני to cover that loss of up to half.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא – נָטְרִי עַד נִיסָן, וּמְזַבְּנִי;
phrases.english: For everyone waits until Nisan, and then sells;
but this one, since he needs money,
sells at the current price.
Up to half, it is its way to drop;
more than that, it is not its way to drop.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נָטְרִי עַד נִיסָן וּמְזַבְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer that began in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the size of the limit: the most that land can lose in value.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may take מעשר עני up to half his land's value, because that is the most he loses by selling in תשרי.

steps.title: אביי applies the seasonal idea to damages
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that in damages the same seasonal situation applies: the injured person's legal right is to collect from עידית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here too, regarding damages, his law is to collect from the best land.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now returns to his own question about נזקין and starts to apply רבה's seasonal idea. This line sets up the explanation that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's point is that the damages case can be understood with the same ניסן/תשרי picture. The basic rule is that the injured person collects from עידית. How much land he gets depends on the season's price, and the גמרא is about to spell that out.

phrases.english: And here too, regarding damages,
his law is with the best land;
phrases.notes: "His" means the injured person. He has the right to be paid from the damager's best land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי נִזָּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבה's seasonal answer about מעשר עני and starts applying it to אביי's own question about נזקין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison: a similar seasonal distinction is applied to damages.
steps.terutzMaskana: The injured person's basic right is payment from עידית, and the season affects how much he receives. Step 5 spells this out.

steps.title: If the injured person asks for medium-quality land, it is valued at the future price
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his damages case. Taking עידית gets today's low valuation. Asking for more בינונית instead gets the future, higher valuation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the injured person says, 'Give me a bit more medium-quality land instead,' the one who caused the damage can answer: 'If you take what the law gives you (best land), take it at today's price. If not, take it at the higher price that is coming.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his example. He shows how the cheap-now and expensive-later pricing matters when paying for damages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The injured person's legal right is the best land (עידית), valued at the current low תשרי price, so he gets a lot of land. If he gives up that right and asks for medium land (בינונית), the payer may value it at the higher ניסן price, so he gets less land. This is how אביי settles his contradiction: 'מיטב' describes the basic right, and 'ישיב' (any payment) covers the case where the injured person waives it.

keyTerms.meaning: The higher price that is coming later

phrases.english: And if he says to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the injured person, talking to the one who damaged him.

phrases.english: Give me medium-quality land, a little more of it;
he can say to him: If you take according to your legal right,
take it at today's price,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – שְׁקֹיל כִּי יוּקְרָא דִּלְקַמֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and if not, take it at the higher price that is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִיהוּ: הַב לִי בֵּינוֹנִית טְפֵי פּוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's damages case that began in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two phrases: 'מיטב' is the injured person's basic right (עידית at today's price). 'ישיב' covers the case where he gives up that right and takes other land, valued at the future ניסן price.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's 'מיטב שדהו' (pay only from the best land) seems to clash with 'ישיב' (pay with anything of value).
steps.terutzMaskana: In damages, giving up עידית for בינונית means the land is valued at the higher future price

steps.title: This would weaken the injured person, whom the תורה favors
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב objects: the תורה gave injured people the best land to help them. אביי's rule ends up penalizing them if they accept lesser land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב challenged this: If so, you have weakened injured people when it comes to medium and poor land. The Merciful One said 'from the best,' and you are saying they can't even take medium or poor land without losing out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks אביי's example. He says it cannot be right, because it works against the injured person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's word מיטב ('the best') was meant to give the injured person extra power. Under אביי's case, an injured person who agrees to medium or poor land is punished with the higher valuation. A rule meant to help him should not make every other option worse for him.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, הוֹרַעְתָּ כֹּחָן שֶׁל נִזָּקִין
phrases.english: If so, you have weakened the power of injured people
regarding medium and poor land,
for the Merciful One said 'from the best,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מִבֵּינוֹנִית וְזִיבּוּרִית נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: and you say: not from medium and poor land either!
phrases.notes: He means: not without losing value. That defeats the תורה's goal of helping him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אִם כֵּן, הוֹרַעְתָּ כֹּחָן שֶׁל נִזָּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's damages example from steps 4–5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's application of seasonal pricing to damages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה's 'מיטב' strengthens injured people. A rule that penalizes them for accepting lesser land goes against that purpose.

steps.title: Better to compare the case to a lender
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב moves the idea to a בעל חוב. A lender's right is בינונית, valued at today's price. If he asks for זיבורית, it is valued at the future price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: If we need a comparison, we compare it to a lender. A lender's right is medium land. If he says, 'Give me a bit more poor land instead,' the borrower can answer: 'If you take what the law gives you, take it at today's price. If not, take it at the higher price that is coming.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב offers his own replacement for אביי's case. He uses a lender instead of an injured person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same pattern as before, one level down. A lender is normally paid from בינונית, so asking for זיבורית means giving up his right. Since the תורה did not give lenders a special boost the way it gave injured people 'מיטב', this does not seem to clash with any פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
If there is something to compare it to,
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבה's seasonal-price idea from steps 2–3.

phrases.english: we compare it to a lender;
a lender's legal right is medium land.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמַר לֵיהּ: הַב לִי זִיבּוּרִית טְפֵי פּוּרְתָּא,
phrases.english: And if he says to him: Give me poor land, a little more of it,
he can say to him: If you take according to your legal right,
take it at today's price,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – שְׁקֹיל כִּי יוּקְרָא דִּלְקַמֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and if not, take it at the higher price that is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אִי אִיכָּא לְדַמּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's damages case, רב אחא בר יעקב replaces it with a lender case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the idea to a different legal setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seasonal-price rule applies to damages
steps.terutzMaskana: It fits a lender: giving up בינונית for זיבורית means the land is valued at the higher future price

steps.title: This would discourage people from lending
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא objects: penalizing lenders this way would make people stop lending.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב איקא, challenged this: If so, you have locked the door in front of borrowers. The lender will say: 'If I still had my money, I could buy land at today's price. Now that my money is with you, I have to take land at the higher future price?!'
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge, now against רב אחא בר יעקב's lender case. In step 9, the same challenger offers a different case instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender complains that lending put him at a disadvantage. With cash in hand he could buy at the cheap תשרי price, but because he lent it out he gets the expensive ניסן valuation. If lending hurts lenders, people will refuse to lend, and borrowers will be shut out.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Locking the door before borrowers' is not about hurting borrowers directly. A rule that hurts lenders makes them stop lending, and that is what shuts the door on borrowers.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, נָעַלְתָּ דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לֹוִין –
phrases.english: If so, you have locked the door in front of borrowers,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: אִילּוּ הֲווֹ לִי זוּזֵי,
phrases.english: for he (the lender) will say to him: If I had my money,
I would buy at today's price;
now that my money is with you,
should I take at the higher price that is coming?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: אִם כֵּן, נָעַלְתָּ דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לֹוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lender case that רב אחא בר יעקב offered in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's application of seasonal pricing to a lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Valuing the lender's land at the future high price makes lending a losing deal. Lenders will stop lending, and borrowers will be locked out.

steps.title: The seasonal-price rule fits a woman collecting her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the rule belongs to כתובת אשה. Her right is the worst land (זיבורית) at today's price. If she asks for a little less בינונית instead, it is valued at the future, higher price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא son of רב איקא said: If we need something to compare this rule to, compare it to a woman's כתובה. A woman collects her כתובה from the worst land. If she says, 'Give me a little less of the middle-quality land,' he can answer: 'If you take what you are entitled to, take it at today's price. If not, take it at the higher price of later on.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having just knocked down the lender version, רב אחא בריה דרב איקא offers his own case where the seasonal-price rule fits: a woman collecting her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule as in steps 5 and 7, now moved to a third kind of collector. A woman's set right is the lowest land, זיבורית, at today's low price. If she asks for better land than her right, בינונית, the husband can make her accept the future, higher price, so she gets less land.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband owes his wife if he divorces her or dies
The higher price of later on
To compare one case to another

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
If there is something to compare it to,
phrases.notes: "It" means the rule from the earlier steps: today's price for your right, the future price if you ask for something else.

phrases.english: we compare it to a woman's marriage contract;
for a woman's marriage contract, her legal right is from the worst land,
and if she says to him:
Give me middle-quality land, a little less of it;
he can say to her:
If you take according to your right,
take at the current value,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording. It makes 'take' a command spoken to a woman.

phrases.english: and if not,
take at the higher price of later on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the lender case in step 8, the same speaker gives a new case where the rule works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the rule to a different case where it causes no problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seasonal-price rule might apply to damages or to a lender.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule fits a woman collecting her כתובה: her right is זיבורית at today's price, and asking for בינונית means the future price.
steps.whyThisMatters: It finishes the search for a real case of the seasonal-price rule, so the גמרא can go back to its original problem.

steps.title: The original difficulty is still unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that, whatever the outcome of the side discussion, the first problem about how an injurer pays has come back. Steps 11–13 answer it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, it is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion about seasonal prices and goes back to the original question, which that discussion did not solve. Steps 11–13 bring new answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seasonal-price idea was meant to solve the earlier difficulty about paying for damages. Since that idea ended up applying only to a כתובה, the problem about damages is back. This short line sets up רבא's new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty; the question still stands

phrases.english: Either way, it is still a difficulty!
phrases.notes: This points back to the original problem about how an injurer pays, which the side discussion did not solve.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the side discussion and reopens the main problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's contradiction between 'מיטב שדהו' (only the best land) and 'ישיב' (any form of payment)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seasonal-price answer turned out to fit only a כתובה, so it no longer answers the question about damages.

steps.title: Whatever he pays with must be the best of its kind
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'the best' does not limit payment to land. Whatever the injurer pays with, he must give the best of that thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whatever he gives him, he must give from the best.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new answer to the original difficulty: the injurer may pay with anything, but it must be his best of that kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'מיטב' as a quality rule, not a type rule. Payment does not have to be land. Whatever item is used must be the best of its kind.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whatever he gives him,
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who did the damage, paying the person he hurt.

phrases.english: he must give him from the best.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֹּל דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty reopened in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the word 'מיטב' as being about quality, not about land
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מיטב' means the injurer must pay with his best land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment may be in any form, as long as it is the best of that kind.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying land is never used. He is saying 'the best' is about how good the payment is, not which kind of thing it is.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'the best of his field'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the פסוק says 'the best of his field,' which sounds like it is talking about land specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'the best of his field'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא by quoting the exact words of the פסוק, which mention a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מיטב' only meant 'the best of whatever you pay with,' why does the תורה say 'of his field'? The word 'field' seems to tie the rule to land, which goes against רבא's broad reading.

phrases.english: But isn't "the best of his field" written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״מֵיטַב שָׂדֵהוּ״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבא's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'מיטב' applies to any kind of payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'of his field,' which seems to limit 'the best' to land.

steps.title: All movables count as 'best'; only land must be top quality
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explain that any movable item counts as 'the best' because it can always be sold somewhere. Land is the exception, so if the injurer pays with land, it must be his best land, which a buyer will want.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע came back from the study hall, they explained it this way: every kind of item counts as 'the best,' because if it can't be sold here, it can be sold in another town. Land is different. With land he must give from the best, so that a buyer will jump to buy it.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the question in step 12, the גמרא drops רבא's reading. It brings a different explanation from רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע that solves the original difficulty another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable things can always be carried to another town and sold, so they already work as 'the best' for the injured person. Land cannot be moved, and poor land may never find a buyer. So the words 'the best of his field' are aimed at land in particular: if he pays with land, it must be good land that sells easily.

keyTerms.meaning: All things, every kind of item

steps.whatToRemember: Movables always count as 'best' because they can be sold anywhere. Only land has to be the injurer's best quality, so that it can be sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles how both parts of the פסוק fit together. 'He shall pay' allows any item of value, and 'the best of his field' sets the rule for land.

phrases.english: Rather, when Rav Pappa came

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, from the study hall,
they explained it:
all things count as 'the best,'
phrases.notes: He means movable things. They are fine to pay with, even if they aren't top quality.

phrases.english: because if it cannot be sold here,
it can be sold in another town;
except for land,
where he must give him from the best,
so that a buyer will jump at it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב, פָּרְשׁוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 12 against רבא and replaces his reading. Movables always count as 'best,' and 'the best of his field' applies only to land.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the meaning of 'best': movables are always good enough, and land must be the best quality.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's reading, that 'מיטב' means every kind of payment must be the best of its kind, cannot fit the words 'of his field'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any movable item counts as 'best.' The words 'of his field' set the quality rule for land, so that it can be sold easily.

steps.title: Is 'best land' measured against the payer's own fields or land in general?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אבא from אקרוניא asks רבי אבא: when the court judges whether land counts as 'best,' does it compare it to the owner's other fields or to land everywhere?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אבא from אקרוניא asked רבי אבא: when the court estimates the land, does it estimate based on his own fields, or based on the land of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. Now that we know land must be 'the best,' someone asks what the land is being compared to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field could be the best one this person owns but still only average compared to land in general. The question is which comparison the court uses. The answer decides which field the injurer must hand over.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question put to a teacher)
They (the court) estimate the value or quality

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Abba asked
from Akronya, of Rabbi Abba:
phrases.notes: Akronya is where רב שמואל בר אבא came from, and he's putting the question to רבי אבא.

phrases.english: when they estimate,
do they estimate based on his own,
phrases.notes: His own other fields: is this the best field compared to the rest of what he owns?

phrases.english: or do they estimate based on that of the world?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא מֵאַקְרוֹנְיָא מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that land payment must be 'the best' and asks how 'best' is measured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the court judges 'best' land by comparing it to the payer's own fields or to land in general.

steps.title: No question according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question does not come up according to רבי ישמעאל, who holds the court measures by the injured person's land.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי ישמעאל you don't need to ask, because he says we estimate based on the injured person's land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question by showing one opinion where it does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that 'best' is measured by the injured person's fields. The injurer pays land as good as the injured person's best. So the payer's own fields, and land in the world, don't matter, and there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: You don't need to ask; the question doesn't come up

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yishmael
you need not ask,
since he says we estimate based on the injured person's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the question from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, 'best' is measured by the injured person's land, so the question does not come up.

steps.title: The question applies according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question only comes up according to רבי עקיבא, who holds the court measures by the injurer's land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you do need to ask is according to רבי עקיבא, who says we estimate based on the injurer's land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which opinion the question really belongs to. This sets up the next part of the discussion, which continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא measures 'best' by the injurer's land. That brings back the question from step 14: is it the best compared to his own other fields, or compared to land in general?

keyTerms.meaning: Where you do need to ask
The one who caused the damage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רבי ישמעאל measures by the injured person's (ניזק) land, and רבי עקיבא measures by the injurer's (מזיק) land.

phrases.english: Where you do need to ask
is according to Rabbi Akiva,
who says we estimate based on the injurer's,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes narrowing the question: it is not asked according to רבי ישמעאל, only according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, who measures by the injurer's land, we still need to know whether 'best' means compared to his own fields or to land in general.

steps.title: The question spelled out: what does 'his field' rule out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the two sides of רב שמואל בר אבא's question. Does 'his field' only rule out measuring by the injured person's land, or does it also rule out measuring by land in the world at large?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? The תורה said 'the best of his field.' Is that only to exclude measuring by the injured person's land? Or perhaps it also excludes measuring by land in the world at large?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what רב שמואל בר אבא is asking, by laying out the two possible ways to read the word 'his.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from רבי עקיבא that we do not measure by the ניזק's land. The question is whether 'his field' also means we ignore the world's standard and only compare to the injurer's own fields. If so, the injurer's best field is enough, even if it is average land by normal standards.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
The world, meaning land in general

phrases.english: What [is the answer]?
'The best of his field,' the Merciful One said:
is it to exclude [the land] of the injured party;
or perhaps, to exclude [the land] of the world as well?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? ״מֵיטַב שָׂדֵהוּ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question that steps 14-16 set up, now stated according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'his field' excludes only the injured party's land, or also excludes the world-wide standard of land.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the פסוק says 'his field,' so measure by his own land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that since the תורה says 'his field,' we cannot measure by land in the world at large. The injurer's own best field is what counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The תורה says 'the best of his field,' and you suggest we measure by the world's land?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question. The word 'his' clearly points to the injurer's own fields, not to land in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא reads 'his' as fully limiting. It rules out both the ניזק's land and the world's standard. So whatever is the best land this injurer owns counts as 'מיטב.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
The world, meaning land in general

phrases.english: He said to him,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אבא answering רב שמואל בר אבא.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said: 'The best of his field,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ בְּשֶׁל עוֹלָם הֵן שָׁמִין?!
phrases.english: and you say they appraise by [the land] of the world?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, רַחֲמָנָא אָמַר: ״מֵיטַב שָׂדֵהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We measure only by the injurer's own land. 'His field' rules out the world-wide standard too.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא: when a person owns only one grade of land
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אבא challenges רבי אבא with a ברייתא. It starts by saying that if a person owns only one grade of land, every creditor collects from that grade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If he has only superior land, everyone collects from the superior land. If only intermediate, everyone collects intermediate. If only inferior, everyone collects inferior.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר אבא begins a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup: it is the first part of the source, and the problem comes from how it labels land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sorts land into three grades: superior, intermediate and inferior. If the person owns only one grade, everyone (the ניזק, a creditor, a wife's כתובה) collects from it. Notice that the ברייתא gives a fixed name to each grade no matter what else this person owns.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רב שמואל בר אבא is challenging רבי אבא from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he has only superior land,
all of them collect from the superior land.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the injured person, a lender, and a wife collecting her כתובה.

phrases.english: [If only] intermediate, all of them collect intermediate.
[If only] inferior, all of them collect inferior.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא עִידִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רבי אבא's answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's ruling that 'best' is judged only by the injurer's own land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא labels land grades by a fixed standard. This suggests the grades are judged against land in general.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: owning two or three grades of land
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains who collects from which grade when a person owns several grades. Damages get the higher land, a creditor gets intermediate, and a כתובה gets the lowest available.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has superior, intermediate and inferior land: damages from superior, a creditor from intermediate, a כתובה from inferior. Superior and intermediate: damages from superior, creditor and כתובה from intermediate. Intermediate and inferior: damages and creditor from intermediate, כתובה from inferior.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of cases. On the next amud, the גמרא explains exactly how it challenges רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at the last case. The person owns only intermediate and inferior land, so intermediate is his best. Yet the ברייתא still calls it 'intermediate,' as if graded by an outside standard. That is the point that seems hard for רבי אבא's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא itself states the question. It is only the source. The actual problem for רבי אבא is spelled out in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.whatToRemember: Damages are paid from the best land, a creditor from the middle, and a כתובה from the lowest. The ברייתא's fixed labels set up a challenge to measuring 'best' only by the injurer's own land.

phrases.english: If he had superior, intermediate and inferior [land]:
damages, from superior,
and a creditor, from intermediate,
and a woman's כתובה, from inferior.
[If he had] superior and intermediate:
damages, from superior,
a creditor and a woman's כתובה, from intermediate.
[If he had] intermediate and inferior:
damages and a creditor, from intermediate,
and a woman's כתובה, from inferior.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ לוֹ עִידִּית וּבֵינוֹנִית וְזִיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that step 19 began, as the basis for the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's view that 'best' is measured by the injurer's own land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the intermediate-and-inferior case, the injurer's best land is still called 'intermediate.' This implies grading by a general standard, and the גמרא will draw this out next.
